sections.html:
The Collier County clerk and comptroller keeps the county's Official Records. The clerk's records search page lists the categories: Official Records (mortgages, deeds, plat maps, condominium declarations and marriage licenses), court records, board minutes, foreclosure judgments, the tax deeds list and Value Adjustment Board files.

The Official Records portal is a separate search tool linked from that page. Search it by party name or document type to see whether a mortgage, lien or earlier deed sits on a Naples, Marco Island or Immokalee property. The clerk's custodian of public records takes requests at 3315 Tamiami Trail East, Suite 102, Naples, FL 34112, phone (239) 252-2646.

sections.h2: What the clerk keeps for a house sale
sections.html:
Any instrument that has to be recorded to protect a buyer lands in the clerk's Official Records, and a title company searches that file before a Collier County closing. Typical contents:

  • Warranty, quit claim and other deeds that moved title to the current owner
  • Mortgages and the satisfactions that release them
  • Plat maps and condominium declarations for the subdivision or building
  • Lis pendens notices filed when a foreclosure case begins

The clerk also posts the foreclosure sale list and the tax deeds list, so a title problem tied to a court case or unpaid tax usually shows up under one of those headings.

Recording in Naples starts at $10.00 for page one of a letter or legal size instrument, then $8.50 for each further page. The statute behind the base charge sets $5.00 and $4.00, and the county's page adds the extra per-page charges the statute allows. The lines below are the ones most sellers meet.

Lis pendens recordings have their own line: $5.00 for the first page, $4.00 for each added page and $1.00 for each name past four. In person, the office takes money orders, cashier's checks, personal checks, cash or cards, and cards add a 3.5% processing fee.

sections.h2: Documentary stamp tax on a deed
sections.html:
State tax on a deed is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration. The Collier clerk collects it at the counter or online as the deed is recorded, and rounds the amount up to the nearest hundred.

The Department of Revenue treats each party to the document as answerable for the tax, whoever agrees to pay. Consideration takes in cash, a discharged debt and any mortgage on the parcel, assumed or not. Deeds are taxable recorded or not, and warranty, special warranty, quit claim, trustee's and life estate deeds are all on the taxable list. A probate personal representative's deed is not taxable.

Mortgages and notes have separate rates. The state sets 35 cents per $100 of the amount secured, matching the clerk's mortgage line, and caps the tax on a note at $2,450 with no cap on mortgages. Your closing agent can run the final figure.

Yes, the Collier clerk accepts e-recording through its own sign-in and through partner vendors. Members of the public can register for a public account, submit from a computer, tablet or phone and pay by card, with a 4% fee from the card processor on top of standard recording fees.

  • Scans must be black and white at 300 dpi, on 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 pages.
  • Business customers can open an escrow account funded by electronic transfer, check or cash, with a $0.50 bank fee per transfer up to $75,000.
  • The clerk lists two partner networks, and their services may add processing fees.

A document counts as recorded once the clerk enters it into the Official Records. The office can't promise same-day recording for mail or electronic submissions, so a time-sensitive document belongs at the main office, where it is recorded while you wait.

Pull your own chain of title first, because a clean search saves days at closing. Look up the deed you received, then every instrument recorded against your name since.

  • A mortgage with no recorded satisfaction after payoff
  • Claims of lien from contractors or an owners' association
  • Judgments recorded against a seller with a similar name
  • Recorded easements shown on the plat

A certification costs $2.00 and a search $2.00 per name, instrument or year, so a certified copy of a paid-off mortgage is cheap next to a delayed closing. Heirs selling an inherited house should ask the clerk's probate division which court file covers the estate, since a personal representative's deed can only follow the court's authority.

Unpaid real estate tax becomes a tax certificate, and its holder can later seek a tax deed that the clerk auctions. The clerk's tax deeds list shows which Collier parcels have reached that stage.

Under state law a tax deed application can be filed once two years have run from April 1 of the year the certificate was issued. The county tax collector's site links to an online certificate sale. When you sell, gather the collector's payoff and the clerk's lien search side by side and hand both to the closing agent. Our Collier County property tax guide covers the billing side.

sections.h2: Researching a parcel before you list
sections.html:
The Collier County Property Appraiser runs the parcel search and posts public data files for the whole county or a smaller area at no charge. Pair a parcel lookup with an Official Records search by owner name, and you can match the legal description on your deed against what the appraiser shows.

Before listing, verify three items: the owner name spelled the same on the deed and the tax roll, any mortgage with no recorded satisfaction, and any recorded notice from a court case. A mismatch is easier to fix with the clerk before an offer arrives than during closing week.

sections.h2: If you record the deed yourself
sections.html: Prepare the signed deed, the parcel number, and payment for the recording charge and stamp tax. Confirm the legal description matches your prior deed, and ask the office for a receipt. After recording, request a copy showing the recording stamp and keep it with your closing file. Buyers and lenders expect that stamped copy, and a cash buyer will want it too, since there is no lender to chase it for them.

faqs.q: Who records deeds in Collier County?
faqs.a: The Collier clerk and comptroller. The Recording Department is at 3315 Tamiami Trail East, Suite 102, Naples, and takes calls at (239) 252-2646.

faqs.q: What does the Collier clerk charge for the first page of a document?
faqs.a: Page one costs $10.00 and later pages $8.50 each, for letter or legal size instruments. Oversize plats cost $30.00 for page one and $15.00 for every page after.

faqs.q: What is the doc stamp rate on a Collier County deed?
faqs.a: $0.70 per $100.00 of consideration, rounded up to the nearest hundred. Florida makes all parties to the document liable, so the contract decides who pays it.

faqs.q: Can I use a credit card at the Collier recording desk?
faqs.a: Yes, in person, with a 3.5% processing fee on each transaction. E-recording with a card carries a 4% fee from the card processor.

faqs.q: Will e-recorded documents be recorded the same day?
faqs.a: Not always. The clerk processes mailed and electronic submissions as time permits and can't guarantee same-day recording, so bring urgent documents to the main office.
